Remark
[dimension bound for conjugate multiplicity]

↗ rem:dc-ch5-2-2 1. ch5:3.2If $\dim M=n$, the Jacobi fields along $\gamma $ that vanish at $0$ form an $n$-dimensional space. A conjugate point along a nonconstant geodesic has multiplicity at most $n-1$.
Proof

\sketch The initial-derivative map $J\mapsto J'(0)$ identifies this space with $T_{\gamma (0)}M$; in particular, fields $J_i$ vanishing at $0$ are linearly independent exactly when the vectors $J_i'(0)$ are. At a positive endpoint, the field $t\gamma '(t)$ of section 1 does not vanish, so the kernel of endpoint evaluation is a proper subspace and has dimension at most $n-1$.

□
